rationale: Round 0 built and passed, so this round escalates obfuscation strength while keeping selectivity via the cost dimensions. The sample is tiny (4 functions, ~1 KB text) with a compute-hot sieve loop, so SUB, IBR, and ICALL get the highest Security/Diversity weights (0.80-0.85) because they add strong static-analysis resistance at low per-iteration cost; their moderate RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights let the selector still skip them on the most cost-sensitive inner-loop regions. FLA and BCF are raised (0.75-0.80 security) to restructure control flow of main and sieve, but with the highest RuntimeCost (0.70-0.80) and SizeCost weights so the flattening/bogus-block expansion is applied selectively rather than uniformly, protecting the hot filtering loop from multiplicative overhead in this size-constrained binary. SPLIT stays a supporting pass (0.55 security) to create more function-level targets for the others at near-zero risk. IGV keeps moderate weights: this program has few globals (iostream init, statics), so its payoff is limited but its cost is also low, making it a cheap diversity add.
